mechanism_narrative: A sustained month-over-month increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates strengthening labor market conditions that directly boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days without regime dependence.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate increase above 4.5% signals imminent monetary tightening, which immediately compresses equity valuations through higher discount rates, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS indicate an aggressive monetary response to accelerating inflation, which triggers equity sell-offs and produces negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising CPIAUCSL and rising FEDFUNDS fails to predict negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of cases (Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows).

mechanism_narrative: In a supply shock regime, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 indicates manufacturing contraction, which reduces corporate output capacity and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO falls below 100.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in housing starts (HOUST) reflects robust consumer demand for residential construction, which typically precedes higher corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST increases by at least 0.5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts decline below 1900 thousand units signals weakening consumer demand, which immediately reduces retail and construction sector activity, causing negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when HOUST falls below 1900.

mechanism_narrative: In a high inflation regime, a CPIAUCSL reading above 200 triggers aggressive monetary policy expectations, which depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 200.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in PAYEMS and decreases in UNRATE indicate a tightening labor market that boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising PAYEMS and falling UNRATE fails to predict positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of cases (Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows).
